content:
The image shows a corn ear with husks pulled back, revealing kernels covered in a distinctly **green/teal-colored mold**. Key observations:
- Affected part: ear (cob/kernels)
- Color: blue-green to teal mold covering a large portion of the kernels
- Texture: appears powdery/fuzzy
- Some white mycelium also visible at the tip

This is clearly an ear rot. The green coloration narrows it significantly:
- **Trichoderma** ear rot: characteristic bright blue-green to teal mold — matches well
- **Aspergillus** ear rot: olive-green/yellow-green, typically more yellowish
- **Gibberella**: pink/red
- **Diplodia**: white/gray

The blue-green teal color is the hallmark of Trichoderma ear rot, distinguishing it from Aspergillus (which skews more olive/yellow-green).
